title: Christianity and Secularism
welcome_lead: Walk the streets of secularising Europe with Nietzsche, Freud, and Dawkins, and meet Christian thinkers who took up the challenge.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on Christianity and secular challenges: Nietzsche, Freud, Dawkins, and Christian responses.

walkthroughs.body_html: Feuerbach's Essence of Christianity (1841) argued that theology is anthropology: God is humanity's projection. Marx famously called religion 'the opium of the people' in his 1844 introduction to Hegel's Philosophy of Right - both consolation and ideology masking exploitation. Nietzsche,The Gay Science (1882) section 125, narrated the madman's proclamation that 'God is dead. and we have killed him'.

Freud's The Future of an Illusion (1927) and Civilization and its Discontents (1930) treated religion as wish-fulfilment, projecting paternal authority onto the cosmos. Richard Dawkins's The God Delusion (2006), Daniel Dennett's Breaking the Spell, Sam Harris's The End of Faith, and Christopher Hitchens's God Is Not Great mounted the New Atheist polemic.

Karl Barth's Church Dogmatics distinguishes religion (human projection) from revelation, granting Feuerbach his critique of religion while preserving the Word of God. Alister McGrath replies to Dawkins in The Dawkins Delusion? (2007). Charles Taylor's A Secular Age (2007) charts a more nuanced narrative than simple decline. Habermas advocates dialogue between secular and religious citizens.

Five distinct arguments for God's existence: from motion, causation, contingency, gradation of being, and final causes/teleology — collectively forming Aquinas's natural theology, not a single argument.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five steps of one cosmological argument.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: Christians believe in three different gods.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
